name: Goroka
note: Town: provincial capital of Eastern Highlands and the base for the Goroka Show, Asaro Mudmen and Mount Michael; the region's main hub (base).

name: Mount Hagen
note: Town: provincial capital of Western Highlands and the regional air hub (Kagamuga Airport); base for Kuk, Hagen Show, Baiyer River and Mount Hagen Market.

name: Kainantu
note: Town: market town on the Highlands Highway with the Eastern Highlands Cultural Centre and pottery; a stop between Lae and Goroka.

name: Mendi
note: Town: provincial capital of Southern Highlands; gateway to Lake Kutubu and Mount Giluwe, with a Friday and Saturday market.

name: Kundiawa
note: Town: capital of Simbu (Chimbu) Province; the departure point for the Mount Wilhelm climb, reached from Keglsugl.

name: Wabag
note: Town: capital of Enga Province; base for Yuo Falls, the Laiagam salt ponds and the Taekanda Cultural Centre.

name: Tari
note: Town: capital of Hela Province and base for the Huli wigmen, Tari Basin and Ambua Lodge. No Wikivoyage article exists (404).

name: Banz
note: Town: Jiwaka town on the Highlands Highway, known for its market (Banz Market).

name: Minj
note: Town: Jiwaka's interim administrative seat (named by the tourism board's Jiwaka page). No Wikipedia article found under this title.

name: Laiagam
note: Town: main town of Lagaip District in Enga; site of the Laiagam Botanical Gardens and salt ponds.

name: Ukarumpa
note: Settlement: missionary community (Summer Institute of Linguistics) in Eastern Highlands; named by Wikivoyage as a place of interest, not a visitor attraction as such.

name: Ialibu
note: Town: Ialibu township in Southern Highlands, known for its basket weaving and the Ialibu Museum; the tourism board names it as a place to get a feel for Southern Highlands life.

name: Okapa
note: Town: district centre in Eastern Highlands; the tourism board names treks to waterfalls and forest lookouts near it.

name: Lufa
note: District: Lufa in Eastern Highlands, named for its cave paintings and eco-trails. No Wikipedia article found under this title.

name: Mount Wilhelm
coordinates_source: osm natural=peak node (MEDIUM; Wikipedia coordinates are rounded)
note: Mountain: Papua New Guinea's highest peak (4,509 m), climbed by guided treks from Keglsugl (Simbu) or Ambullua (Western Highlands).

name: Mount Giluwe
note: Mountain: second-highest peak in PNG (4,368 m), a shield volcano with guided climbs, in Southern Highlands.

name: Mount Ialibu
note: Mountain: 3,465 m peak near Ialibu with tracks around it, named by the tourism board. No separate Wikipedia article found (the Ialibu article is about the town).

name: Mount Hagen (volcano)
note: Mountain: extinct 3,765 m volcano 24 km northwest of Mount Hagen town; Wikivoyage suggests climbing it, with little visitor infrastructure.

name: The Sugarloaf
note: Mountain: peak near Mount Hagen that Wikivoyage suggests climbing; little known, no article found.

name: Mount Kabangama
note: Mountain: highest peak in the Kubor Range (first summited 2018), southeast of Mount Hagen; Wikivoyage lists it as a climb. No Wikipedia article found.

name: Mount Michael
note: Mountain: cloud-forest hill near Goroka with hiking trails and highland views. The Wikipedia title Mount Michael is the South Sandwich Islands volcano, so it is not used.

name: Lake Kutubu
note: Lake: 800 m upland lake, about 50 km southwest of Mendi, with Ramsar status and endemic fish; reached by road and boat.

name: Lake Piunde
coordinates_source: osm natural=water (lake centroid, in water is correct)
note: Lake: one of the twin alpine lakes (Piunde and Aunde) on the Keglsugl route up Mount Wilhelm, with huts. Named only in the Wikipedia article on the mountain; no counted source yet.

name: Toi Wara Waterfall
note: Waterfall: river and waterfall about four hours from Mount Hagen in Southern Highlands, reached by a steep trail to a cove behind the falls. Wikivoyage describes it as adventurous; no Wikipedia article found.

name: Wasi Falls
note: Waterfall: 100 m fall in a Wildlife Management Area in Southern Highlands, reached on guided tours from Lakwanda. No Wikipedia article found.

name: Yuo Falls
note: Waterfall: falls about a 15-minute hike from Wabag town in Enga Province. No Wikipedia article found.

name: Bisil Kana Waterfall
note: Waterfall: river that bursts out of a mountain face as a 10 m wide cascade in Jiwaka. No Wikipedia article found.

name: Waghi River
note: River: the Waghi River in Jiwaka, named by the tourism board for river crossings and banks. Not a single visitor site.

name: Tagari River
note: River: whitewater river near Tari in Hela Province, named for white-water rafting. No Wikipedia article found.

name: Kuk Early Agricultural Site
note: Archaeological site: UNESCO World Heritage Site of ancient swamp gardens (about 7,000 years old) 12 km northeast of Mount Hagen; visitors need permission to enter.

name: Baiyer River Sanctuary
note: Nature reserve: 740 ha bird sanctuary about 40 km from Mount Hagen, with bird-of-paradise species. Wikipedia lists it as a tourist attraction; no counted source yet.

name: Asaro Mudmen
note: Cultural attraction: masked mud-men performers from the Asaro people, who live in a village near Goroka; the tourism board names the village performances.

name: Eastern Highlands Cultural Centre and Museum
note: Museum: cultural centre and museum at Kainantu, known for its pottery and the Kainantu pottery and weaving markets. No dedicated Wikipedia article found.

name: J.K. McCarthy Museum
note: Museum: Goroka museum on Airport Road with WWII relics, traditional artefacts and 1930s photos of the first Australian patrols into the Highlands. Hours variable per Wikivoyage.

name: Raun Raun Theatre
note: Theatre: performing-arts building in north Goroka styled like a cluster of traditional huts; performances are irregular, so it is mainly a landmark.

name: Goroka Rugby League Field
note: Sports ground: football field opposite the Goroka market where rugby league games are played most days. A local sports venue, no article.

name: Mount Hagen Market
note: Market: main produce market at Kum Road and the Highlands Highway, selling fresh vegetables and some crafts. Trades on working days, no article.

name: Mendi Market
note: Market: Mendi's market, busiest on Fridays and Saturdays, where Imbonggu baskets are sold. A weekend-heavy market, no article.

name: Banz Market
note: Market: the market at Banz, named by the tourism board as the biggest and best market in Jiwaka. Days of trading not given.

name: Kurumul Tea Plantation
note: Plantation: tea estate of about 2,000 ha in Jiwaka where visitors can pick tea leaves. No Wikipedia article found.

name: Jimi District
note: District: Jimi District in north-east Jiwaka, named by the tourism board for its mountain views and culture on a road trip. A district, not a single site.

name: Huli Wigmen
note: Cultural experience: the Huli wigmen of Tari, who can be visited for cultural tours and photos; the people rather than a fixed site.

name: Tari Basin
note: Basin: the Tari Basin, a valley around Tari with the Huli villages and birdwatching around Ambua. A landscape area, not a single site.

name: Ambua Lodge
note: Lodge: traditional Huli-style lodge near Tari, known for birds-of-paradise watching and Huli village tours. A business, listed by the sources as the place to stay for birdwatching.

name: Warili Lodge
note: Lodge: local budget lodge beside Ambua Lodge with birdwatching, per Wikivoyage. A business.

name: Betty's Place Mount Wilhelm
note: Guesthouse: family-run trout and rabbit farm guesthouse at the Mount Wilhelm gateway, a base for the climb. A business.

name: Nambaiyufa Amphitheatre
note: Site: rock paintings and the Keu Caves at the Nambaiyufa Amphitheatre near Chuave, Simbu. No Wikipedia article found.

name: Lufa Cave Paintings
note: Site: ancient rock-art caves in Lufa district, Eastern Highlands. No Wikipedia article found.

name: Kemase Caves
note: Caves: limestone caves with prehistoric paintings at Kemase village in Lufa, visited through Kemase Eco Tourism. No Wikipedia article found.

name: Laiagam Botanical Gardens
note: Garden: botanical gardens at Laiagam with over 100 species of mountain orchids and rhododendrons. No Wikipedia article found.

name: Laiagam Salt Ponds
note: Natural site: salt ponds near Laiagam, named by the tourism board for a visit. No Wikipedia article found.

name: Taekanda Cultural Centre
note: Museum: Enga cultural centre near Wabag with wigs, war shields, masks and a sand-painting workshop. No Wikipedia article found.

name: Western Highlands Cultural Centre
note: Museum: cultural centre in Mount Hagen with a reconstructed village hut and artefacts. No Wikipedia article found.

name: Rondon Ridge
note: Lodge and farm: lodge near Mount Hagen known for strawberries. A business, not a standalone attraction.

name: Magic Mountain Nature Lodge
note: Lodge: nature lodge in Western Highlands named by the tourism board. A business.

name: Kumul Lodge
note: Lodge: landowner-owned ecotourism lodge in Enga built from local materials. A business.

name: Asaro Mudmen Tribal Eco Lodge
note: Lodge: village eco-lodge in Asaro, near the mudmen village. A business.

name: Kemase Eco Tourism Services
note: Tour operator: locally owned village tours in Kemase, Lufa, including its caves. An operator, not a place.

name: Paradise Café
note: Café: Goroka café named by the tourism board as a stop for locals and travellers. A café, not an attraction.

name: Goroka Show
note: Event: annual sing-sing cultural show around 16 September in Goroka; an event, not a permanent place.

name: Hagen Show
note: Event: annual Mount Hagen cultural show held in August or September at the show grounds near the airport; an event, the venue is the grounds.

name: Waghi Show
note: Event: annual Waghi Show held every June in Jiwaka; an event, not a place.

name: Enga Cultural Show
note: Event: annual Enga Cultural Show; an event, not a place.

name: PNG Coffee Festival
note: Event: May festival in Goroka with coffee tastings and barista competitions; an event, not a place. Named only in Wikipedia.
